title: Is This Pop Order Possible?

concept.title: Simulate the stack and pop whenever you can
body: Numbers are pushed on an empty stack in the order of the first list, and at any time you may pop the top. Is the second list a possible **order of the pops**? You can simply **simulate** it: push the numbers in order, and after each push **pop as long as the top equals the next number that has to be popped**.

body.code:
stack = []; j = 0
for x in pushed:
    stack.append(x)
    while stack and stack[-1] == popped[j]:    # pop greedily
        stack.pop(); j += 1
return not stack

body: Popping as early as possible is always safe: if the top is the number you need next, no other order can use it later without blocking. At the end, the order is possible exactly when the stack is empty (everything could be popped in the required order).

statement: The distinct numbers of the first list are pushed on an empty stack in this order. Between the pushes (and after the last one) any number of pops may be done. Print `yes` if the numbers of the second list can be the numbers that are popped, in this order, so that the stack ends up empty; otherwise print `no`. The second list contains the same numbers as the first one.
inputFormat: The second line has the pushed numbers.
The third line has the popped numbers.
constraints: All numbers are different, between 0 and 10^9; the second list is a permutation of the first one.

examples.note: After popping 4 3 5 the top is 2, but 1 is needed: impossible.

hints: Simulate: push the next number, then pop while the top is the number you need.
Keep an index into the popped list.
The answer is yes when the stack is empty at the end.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
pushed = list(map(int, input().split()))
popped = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: The stack is simulated: after every push the top is popped while it equals the next required number. If the stack is empty at the end, the order is possible.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
pushed = list(map(int, input().split()))
popped = list(map(int, input().split()))

stack = []
j = 0
for x in pushed:
    stack.append(x)
    while stack and stack[-1] == popped[j]:
        stack.pop()
        j += 1
print("yes" if not stack else "no")
